name: Amazon Athena
oneLiner: Bytes read off S3 per query. Query count barely matters, unless you buy provisioned capacity by the DPU-hour.
trap: Partitioning and columnar formats are the whole game. DDL and failed queries are free, cancelled queries bill for what they already scanned, and each query rounds up to a 10 MB floor.

name: Amazon Augmented AI (A2I)
oneLiner: Per object routed to a human reviewer, on top of whatever the workforce itself charges.
trap: The Mechanical Turk reward is baked into the usage type, so changing the price per task moves the charge to a different rate code entirely. A2I is now in maintenance and no longer accepts new customers.

name: Amazon Bedrock
oneLiner: On-demand meters input and output tokens. Provisioned Throughput rents model units by the hour.
trap: Provisioned Throughput bills per model unit per hour with zero invocations, with or without a 1- or 6-month commitment. Cache-read and cache-write tokens meter separately; batch runs at a discount.

name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
oneLiner: Runtime rents vCPU and memory by the hour; Gateway, Memory and each built-in tool meter separately.
trap: Runtime charges memory for the whole session but vCPU only while the CPU is busy, so I/O wait is free. Gateway adds a monthly fee per indexed tool, and AgentCore observability lands on your CloudWatch bill instead.

name: Amazon Bio Discovery
oneLiner: A monthly plan bundling a set number of Experiment Units. Extra experiments bill per unit.
trap: Collaborators and result viewing are free, so cost tracks experiments rather than seats. Unit consumption scales with candidate count, sequence length and model choice, and wet-lab orders bill outside the plan.

name: AWS Clean Rooms
oneLiner: Per CRPU-hour of query compute, per GB-month of intermediate tables, and per record for ML and matching.
trap: Each query has a minimum billing duration: sixty seconds for Spark SQL, ten minutes for PySpark. Compute bills whichever member the collaboration names as payer, which can be a data owner rather than the query runner.

name: Amazon CloudSearch
oneLiner: Closed to new customers; instances bill hourly and index rebuilds bill per GB stored.
trap: An IndexDocuments request you trigger yourself is charged against the full size of data already in the domain, so schema tweaks on a big domain hurt. Rebuilds AWS initiates on its own are not charged.

name: Amazon Comprehend
oneLiner: Text is billed in 100-character units with a three-unit floor on every request.
trap: Custom endpoints bill per inference unit per second from the moment you start them until you delete them, documents or no documents. Training bills by the hour and the trained model bills monthly.

name: Amazon Comprehend Medical
oneLiner: Per unit of 100 characters, priced separately for entities, PHI, ICD-10, RxNorm and SNOMED CT.
trap: Every request is rounded up to a 100-character minimum, so a stream of tiny calls costs far more than the raw character count suggests. Entity detection runs several times the rate of PHI detection.

name: AWS Data Exchange
oneLiner: Data senders pay per hour each accepted data grant stays active, plus per GB-month of data stored.
trap: AWS's own fee is trivial next to the third-party data subscription billed through it, which the provider prices and which usually runs on a fixed term you keep paying after you stop querying the data.

name: Amazon DataZone
oneLiner: Per API request, per GB of catalog metadata, plus compute units and recommendation tokens.
trap: The per-user subscription charge went away in November 2024, so cost now tracks compute units and catalog storage rather than seats. Background catalog runs, lineage and AI recommendations all generate requests.

name: Amazon Elastic Transcoder
oneLiner: Gone since November 13, 2025; MediaConvert is the replacement.
trap: AWS discontinued the service on November 13, 2025 and console access went with it. Billing was per minute of output, rounded up to a whole minute per file, SD at half the HD rate, failed transcodes usually free.

name: Amazon EMR
oneLiner: An EMR charge per second on every node, stacked on top of the EC2 and EBS bills.
trap: Long-running clusters keep accruing charges until you shut them down, idle or busy. Auto-terminate transient jobs. EMR Serverless meters vCPU-hours, memory GB-hours and storage instead.

name: AWS Entity Resolution
oneLiner: Per record processed or matched, plus a one-off fee for each data matching workflow you create.
trap: You are billed on records fed in, not on matches found, so sweeping a whole table to catch a few duplicates costs the same as one that matches everything. Provider-based matching bills the records it prepares as well.

name: Amazon Forecast
oneLiner: Closed to new signups; existing users pay per GB imported, per training hour, per thousand data points.
trap: Data points multiply fast. A predictor emits a point for every quantile at every step of the horizon across all series, and explanations multiply that again by the number of attributes explained.

name: Amazon Fraud Detector
oneLiner: Predictions are cheap per call; the deployed model holds the meter open.
trap: Billed training compute hours can exceed elapsed training time, because Fraud Detector picks bigger instances than the baseline spec. A deployed model then bills hourly for hosting until you undeploy it.

name: AWS Glue
oneLiner: Jobs, crawlers and sessions rent DPUs by the second. The Data Catalog bills objects and requests.
trap: Crawler runs carry a ten-minute minimum, so crawling every five minutes bills continuously. ETL jobs have a one-minute minimum. Over-provisioned DPUs cost the same idle as busy.

name: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth
oneLiner: You pay per labeled object, twice over.
trap: Two charges land per object: the Ground Truth service fee and the workforce fee. Mechanical Turk tasks price per worker, so raising workers-per-object for label quality multiplies the human half.

name: AWS HealthOmics
oneLiner: Workflow compute per instance-hour, run storage per GB-hour, sequence stores per gigabase-month.
trap: Sequence store storage meters per gigabase, not per GB, so compression does not save you. Static run storage bills for the whole run at the capacity you provisioned, not the busy part.

name: AWS IoT Analytics
oneLiner: Support ended on December 15, 2025.
trap: While it ran, the same data got metered three ways: per GB through the pipeline, per TB scanned by dataset SQL, and per GB-month for the raw and processed copies kept side by side. Console and resources are gone now.

name: Amazon Interactive Video Service (IVS)
oneLiner: Input hours and viewer output hours, both by the hour; chat adds a per-message charge.
trap: Input hours accrue for as long as you push video at a channel, with zero viewers watching. Output hours are a separate meter that scales with audience, so a test stream left broadcasting overnight still bills.

name: Amazon Kendra
oneLiner: An empty index costs exactly what a busy one costs.
trap: AWS states it plainly: once an index exists you pay for it with zero documents and zero queries, and deleting it is the only way to stop the meter. Kendra also closes to new customers on July 30, 2026.

name: AWS Lake Formation
oneLiner: Permissions and LF-Tags are free. Data filtering and storage optimization are not.
trap: Permissions and LF-Tags cost nothing. The storage optimizer belonged to Governed Tables, shut down at the end of 2024, so optimization now bills through the Glue Data Catalog instead.

name: Amazon Lex
oneLiner: Per request, priced differently for speech and text, and differently again for streaming turns.
trap: In request-and-response mode every single user turn is a separate billable request, so a ten-turn conversation is ten charges. Speech requests cost several times a text request for the same turn.

name: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
oneLiner: KPUs bill by the second for as long as the application is RUNNING.
trap: Every application pays one extra KPU for orchestration and Studio notebooks pay two, and each start carries a ten-minute minimum charge. Running application storage bills per GB-month on top.

name: AWS Elemental MediaConnect
oneLiner: Flows and outputs bill by the hour, and transport-stream data transfer bills per GB on top.
trap: A running flow charges hourly whether or not it is passing traffic, and every output adds its own hourly rate. Only a flow left in standby is free. Reserved outbound bandwidth locks you into a 12-month commitment.

name: AWS Elemental MediaConvert
oneLiner: Per minute of output, times a multiplier for every codec, resolution and feature you turn on.
trap: Billing counts output minutes rather than source minutes. A 10-minute mezzanine encoded into a six-rung ABR ladder bills 60 minutes, and each rung applies its own resolution and frame-rate multiplier.

name: AWS Elemental MediaLive
oneLiner: Every input and output bills by the hour.
trap: Stopping a channel does not take it to zero. MediaLive has an explicit idle-channel charge for stopped channels and an idle charge for push inputs; only pull inputs are free while idle. Delete to stop paying.

name: AWS Elemental MediaPackage
oneLiner: Two per-GB meters: what goes in, and what gets packaged back out.
trap: Live ingest is metered per GB, so a high-bitrate contribution feed costs money before a viewer connects. VOD has no ingest charge at all — only packaging on the way out.

name: AWS Elemental MediaTailor
oneLiner: Ad insertions bill per thousand, but a Channel Assembly channel bills every hour it runs.
trap: Two products share one bill. Ad insertion meters per thousand insertions, while Channel Assembly meters per running channel hour, so a linear channel with no audience still accrues hours. Ad delivery is per GB.

name: Amazon Nova Act
oneLiner: Per agent hour, measured as real elapsed time while a browser automation agent is working.
trap: Parallel agents each run their own clock, so a fleet multiplies the meter even on one workflow. Human-in-the-loop waiting is excluded, but S3 and the browser tooling the agent drives bill separately.

name: Amazon OpenSearch Service
oneLiner: Rent the cluster by the hour plus the storage under it. Searches themselves are free.
trap: Nodes bill around the clock with nobody querying. Classic Serverless collections floor at two OCUs, while NextGen collections scale to zero after ten idle minutes. Node-to-node traffic is free.

name: Amazon Personalize
oneLiner: Ingest bills per GB, training bills per hour, recommendations bill per thousand.
trap: Custom solutions only cost you when you train or ask for recommendations. Use-case optimized recommenders behave differently: each active recommender carries an hourly rate that keeps running with no traffic.

name: Amazon Polly
oneLiner: You pay per character of text synthesized. Generative and long-form voices cost far more than standard.
trap: Speech Marks requests bill at the same per-character rate as audio, so asking for both doubles the text you pay for. Replaying a stored MP3 costs nothing; re-synthesizing the same string charges again.

name: Amazon Q
oneLiner: Named-user seats by the month, plus index units billed by the hour.
trap: Index units accrue hourly regardless of query volume, alongside seats you keep paying for on behalf of dormant users. Embedded and anonymous access bills consumption units per ChatSync call instead.

name: Amazon Quick Suite
oneLiner: A per-user monthly or annual subscription, plus pooled index storage per GB and per-hour agents.
trap: Seats bill for the whole month even if the user never signs in, and the Professional and Enterprise plans add a flat monthly per-account infrastructure fee on top of the seats. Free and Plus plans carry no seat charge.

name: Amazon QuickSight
oneLiner: Now the Quick Sight part of Quick Suite. Seats billed monthly per named user, plus SPICE capacity by the GB.
trap: Author and reader seats bill the full month for someone who never logs in. SPICE is charged per GB-month on top, and the embedded capacity plans buy 30-minute sessions in blocks instead of seats.

name: Amazon Rekognition
oneLiner: Images bill per image, video per minute, custom models per hour while they are up.
trap: A running Custom Labels model bills inference hours with no images going through it, and training bills by the hour as well. Stored face and user vectors carry a monthly charge each.

name: Amazon SageMaker AI
oneLiner: Training stops billing when the job ends. A real-time endpoint bills until you delete it.
trap: An endpoint charges instance-hours from creation to deletion with zero invocations, which is the usual SageMaker surprise. Serverless and asynchronous inference both scale to zero for bursty traffic.

name: Amazon Textract
oneLiner: Per page, at a rate set by which features you ask for.
trap: Forms, Tables and Queries requested together on one page charge a single combined per-page rate, higher than any feature alone. A 200-page PDF is 200 pages, and reprocessing it bills again.

name: Amazon Transcribe
oneLiner: Billed on audio duration in one-second increments, with a fifteen-second floor per request.
trap: Slicing a stream into short clips pays the fifteen-second minimum over and over. Call Analytics, Medical and toxicity detection each carry their own rate on top of plain transcription.

name: Amazon Translate
oneLiner: Source characters, whitespace included.
trap: Every space counts, and translating an unchanged string again bills again, so cache the output. Active Custom Translation runs at four times the standard per-character rate.
